Board of Peace: Privatizing Dependence

Board of Peace showed up at the UN donor conference as the clean, technocratic alternative to UNRWA — and managed to prove it’s just a different kind of dependency factory.

The pitch is simple: stop funding “incitement, terrorism and stagnation,” fund Gaza’s “path to peace and prosperity.” Ambassador Jeff Bartos even called long‑term support for UNRWA “the definition of insanity” — doing the same thing and expecting different results. The entire argument rests on one assumption: that the alternative actually exists in practice and works better.

Under Trump’s plan, the World Bank created an official Gaza reconstruction fund with oversight, reporting and UN blessing. Four months later, its balance is zero. Not a dollar.

 The money that did show up went around the fund into a separate JP Morgan account controlled by Board of Peace itself — a structure that, unlike the Bank fund, is not obliged to disclose its finances to donors, or even to all board members. 

Out of the loudly advertised 17 billion in pledges, only crumbs arrived, from just two of nine “lifetime members”: Morocco (a few million) and the UAE. The other seven haven’t paid.

Now line that up with the actual bill: World Bank, EU and UN estimates put Gaza reconstruction north of 70 billion over a decade. Contracts signed so far: zero. Real spending: an office for Nickolay Mladenov and salaries for technocrats. 

The only thing on schedule is the press release telling the world to divert UNRWA money into this black box.

And who lectures UNRWA about “not breeding dependency”? Donald Trump, lifetime chair of the structure, who just declared 1.4 billion dollars in 2025 crypto income — the largest documented private-venture take by a sitting U.S. president. 

Roughly 635 million of that came as royalties from a meme coin named after himself, which then crashed by about 90 percent. At the same time, his companies were buying stock in private prison firms while ICE detention numbers doubled. That’s the man whose ecosystem now instructs Gaza on sound incentives and responsible aid.

Every accusation thrown at UNRWA boomerangs straight back at Board of Peace.

Dependence? UNRWA keeps refugees alive on external funding, yes. Board of Peace built a structure where two million people’s future hangs on the goodwill of nine “lifetime members” and one opaque account. That’s not ending dependency, that’s privatizing it.

Transparency? UNRWA files budgets, submits to audits, lives under donor committees. Board of Peace designed a bypass around the one institution — the World Bank fund — that comes with public reporting, then asks states to wire money into an account that doesn’t have to show anyone its books.

Stagnation? Critics say UNRWA money doesn’t turn into development. After four months, Board of Peace hasn’t produced a single reconstruction contract, tender or project on the ground. The only concrete output is a letter telling governments to redirect someone else’s budget into its own closed system.

By Bartos’s own phrase, the “definition of insanity” here isn’t keeping UNRWA alive while trying to reform it. It’s the idea of handing 100 million dollars to a body that raised zero on its official fund, refuses to show what’s on its unofficial one, and has yet to deliver anything but slogans.

A body that turned Gaza into a hostage of nine signatures — seven of which are still missing — gives the UN a lecture on not “creating dependence.” 

A body run by a president who literally monetizes his name and a meme coin teaches the world about accountability.

That’s not an exit from the old model. It’s the same dependency, just with a different logo on the transfer.

#USA #UN #UNRWA #Gaza #BoardOfPeace #Trump #WorldBank #aid #war #fakeDemocracy

❗️ XRP price forms multi-month falling wedge near $1 support as liquidations mount 

📣 According to data from cryptonews price, XRP price dropped from around $1.07 on June 25 to $1.01 on June 26, extending its year-to-date decline to more than 40%. The decline accelerated as a $10.8 billion crypto options expiry triggered heavy volatility across digital assets and forced a wave of long liquidations.

⚠️ At the same time, sentiment surrounding the XRP ecosystem weakened after decentralized finance protocol Strobe Finance abruptly announced it would shut down operations.

🔖 The daily chart shows XRP trading at the lower edge of a falling wedge that has contained price action for almost a year. The pattern has compressed between descending resistance and gradually declining support, with the token now sitting close to the wedge’s lower boundary near $1.00.

🔗 Momentum indicators remain weak. The MACD has stayed below its signal line with histogram bars still in negative territory, while the Aroon indicator continues to favor sellers after Aroon Down climbed back toward 100 and Aroon Up remained subdued. Together, the indicators suggest bears still control the short-term trend even as XRP price approaches a historically important support zone.
